structured.answer: According to the page, the cheapest is a פסגות account with the fund "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125" (5112628). With 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month (70,000 ₪ put in), it says I'd have about 86,045 ₪ after ten years, against about 81,000–83,000 ₪ at the big banks. I wouldn't do it without first asking my son or the bank.

stuck.why: The minus signs made me think the funds lose money. Only the note at the bottom said it means falling behind the מדד.

stuck.where: Coloured bars in the account list
stuck.why: The colour key is only at the bottom of the list, far from the bars, and the orange and red look alike to me.
I didn't know where the 7% comes from, or whether 86,045 is certain.

findings.what: Minus signs on every fund (−0.04%, −1,030 ₪). They look like losses, and the explanation comes only at the end of the list.
The colour key is far below the bars, and the orange and red are hard to tell apart.
The same 'לא בחישוב מחיר אחר לצעירים, לחיילים...' text is repeated on almost every row.
The page opens with English letters and 'מדד'. It feels like it isn't meant for someone like me.
Dark background with grey text, and many numbers on every screen
The 86,045 result rests on an assumed 7% a year, and it isn't clear this is only a guess.
The adjustments use sliders, though there are boxes too.
